title: Session room: Spotlight (host-driven global pin)
description: Zoom feature we don't have. Our local Speaker view auto-pins the active speaker locally; Spotlight pins one participant for everyone in the room, persists until the host releases it, and surfaces above the active-speaker logic. LiveKit doesn't have a built-in spotlight primitive, but we can implement it by sending a 'spotlight' data-channel message from the host and having every client treat the named identity as the auto-pin target until cleared. UI: a 'Spotlight for everyone' option in the per-tile host hover menu or in the participants panel's per-row host actions. Track current spotlight in room metadata so latecomers see it on join.
notes: Only build if a real session needs it. Most dharma talks don't — the active-speaker pin works fine. Could be useful for panel discussions or guided meditations where the teacher should stay focused regardless of who speaks.

title: Session room: Mirror video toggle in Settings
description: Zoom shows your self-view mirrored by default (matches the mirror you're used to looking in). We render the raw camera feed. Add a 'Mirror my video' toggle in the Video section of VideoSettingsPanel that applies a CSS scaleX(-1) transform only to the local participant's tile (not their video as published to others). Persist in localStorage under rim-livekit-prefs.
notes: Implementation: pass a 'mirror' boolean from VideoSettingsPanel down to RIMParticipantTile. Tile compares trackRef.participant.identity to room.localParticipant.identity and applies '.rim-tile-wrapper--mirror' class only when match. CSS: .rim-tile-wrapper--mirror .lk-participant-video { transform: scaleX(-1); }.

title: Session room: Test Microphone + Test Speakers in Settings
description: Useful pre-session affordance. Test Microphone: 5-second VU-meter showing input volume. Test Speakers: plays a short bell or chime through the selected output device so user can confirm they'll hear the session. Both live in the Audio section of VideoSettingsPanel below the device dropdowns.
notes: Use getUserMedia({ audio: { deviceId: selectedMicId } }) for the test mic; pipe MediaStreamSource through AnalyserNode for VU. Test speakers: a short asset bundled in /public/sounds/, played via Audio element with .setSinkId(selectedSpeakerId) to honor the chosen output.

title: Session room: harden host tag against client spoofing
description: Currently host: true is seeded into participant metadata at token-issue time. The token grants canUpdateOwnMetadata: true so a client can technically rewrite their own metadata in devtools to claim Host. Real host actions (mute, end-for-all) are server-gated via auth() + role + HostAssignment + ProgramTeacher lookup, so this is a UI-only deception risk. To eliminate: route avatar and signal metadata updates through a small server endpoint that calls RoomServiceClient.updateParticipant (server is the only writer), and drop canUpdateOwnMetadata from the token grant. Pattern: POST /api/livekit/metadata with the requested partial; server validates ownership and applies.
notes: Risk-accepted in session 117 for a small trusted Sangha. Worth doing if (a) the community grows large enough that trust no longer covers it, or (b) we ever expose the room beyond authenticated members + key-gated guests. Documented in app/api/livekit/token/route.ts.

title: Session room: chevron 'Audio Settings…' link scrolls to section
description: DevicePickerMenu's bottom links — 'Audio Settings…' and 'Camera Settings…' — open VideoSettingsPanel but don't scroll the panel to the relevant section. Sections are short and the panel body is single-page-scrollable, so this is a minor friction. Accept an optional focusSection: 'audio' | 'video' | 'presence' prop on VideoSettingsPanel; on mount, scrollIntoView the matching section's element.

title: Decide on functional Vercel preview deploys (staging DB or build-only)
description: Session 116 surfaced that Vercel preview builds for non-main branches were failing because prisma/migrate.mjs needs POSTGRES_PRISMA_URL and Vercel preview envs don't inherit production env vars by default. Added a guard at the top of migrate.mjs main() so it skips cleanly when the env is missing — production deploys are unaffected, and preview builds now reach next build without crashing. BUT: the app itself still has no DB at runtime on preview deploys, so any page that hits Prisma will 500 if visited. Two options for the future: (A) provision a small staging/preview Postgres (Neon supports branching — could use a Neon branch as the preview DB, scoped to Vercel's Preview env) and wire its URL to the Preview env scope so previews are functional end-to-end; or (B) accept that previews are build-only checks and not visit-them deployments — in which case maybe configure Vercel to skip preview deploys for most pushes, or just leave the situation as-is. Decision-point: do we want previews to be functional? If yes, set up the branched Neon DB and add it to Vercel Preview env. If no, document the limitation and move on.
notes: Branch pushes are rare in current workflow — Jesse usually goes straight to main. But the moment a branch-based workflow comes back (a real PR, a Claude worktree pass that wants to be reviewed visually before merging), this matters. Not urgent until then. Neon branching is the cleanest path if we go (A) — see https://neon.tech/docs/guides/vercel-overview for the Vercel integration that auto-creates a branch DB per preview deploy.

title: Drop legacy HubConversationThread.status column
description: Session 115 added archivedAt/archivedById to hub_conversation_threads and unified the archive mechanism with HubDocument. The legacy status column (OPEN | CLOSED) is now vestigial: the PATCH handler keeps it in sync with archivedAt for backward compat. Once a few UI reads are migrated to use archivedAt directly, the status column can be dropped. Sites to migrate: components/HubConvThreadClient.tsx:195 (const isClosed = thread.status !== 'OPEN'), components/HubConvClient.tsx:349/440/443/452 (status display + archive toggle buttons), the document conversations POST that initializes status: 'OPEN' on create, and the hub conversations POST that does the same (both can stop writing the field once it's dropped). Then add a migration that drops the column and the @default('OPEN'). Mechanical, low-risk, no rush — purely a model-cleanup item.
notes: Wait until at least one full release cycle passes after session 115 so the in-sync writes have backfilled any rows touched. Then audit grep for remaining 'thread.status' / 'status: "OPEN"' / 'status: "CLOSED"' references.

title: Coordinator-friendly hub content editing for non-host hubs
description: Hub welcomeBody and homeContent are editable inline on the host hub (HostHubHomeClient has an inline edit affordance for coordinators). For the other three hubs (courses, registrar, support), there's no inline editor — coordinators can only edit hub content via /admin/hubs/[slug]/edit, which is strictly ADMIN-only. Session 115 surfaced this when the sidebar Settings link was gated to ADMIN only (matching actual page authorization) — coordinators have no path to edit their hub's welcome message. Two design options: (A) extend HostHubHomeClient's inline edit affordance to all hubs (drop the host-team specific 'Our offerings this month' panel into a hasSchedule branch, keep the welcome editor generic); or (B) build a separate coordinator-scoped /account/hub/[slug]/settings page with welcomeHeadline + welcomeBody + homeContent + conversationCategories editors. Option A is less new UI, keeps editing close to the surface it affects; option B is a cleaner separation between view and edit. Either way, the coordinator-vs-admin distinction needs to be carried through — coordinators edit content fields, admins edit config fields (slug, type, app links, hard-remove coordinators).
notes: Lower urgency than the broader Webflow migration. Currently the only impacted users are coordinators of courses/registrar/support hubs, and those teams aren't yet active. Worth handling before each non-host hub is staffed — but the session 115 welcome seeds buy time.

title: Phase 2: Authenticated CTA states on Webflow Program Detail
description: Extend the ctaHtml pattern on /api/public/programs/[slug] to cover the four authenticated states the RIM Next public detail page already renders: (1) registered — '✓ You’re registered. View your program details'; (2) waitlisted — 'You’re on the waitlist. View details'; (3) open virtual program + logged-in — 'Access Zoom Link in Dashboard →'; (4) open in-person/hybrid + logged-in — 'Simply arrive in person · Zoom link in dashboard'. Requires an authenticated endpoint — /api/member/programs/[slug]/cta-state — that returns either a session: null response (no override) or an ctaHtmlOverride string. rim-connect.js extends to optionally fetch the authenticated endpoint alongside the public one; if it returns an override, it replaces ctaHtml before populating. No Webflow change needed — the existing single-placeholder pattern carries through. Key architectural decision: the auth bridge between Webflow (www.rootedinmindfulness.org) and RIM Next API (rim-next.vercel.app). Three options: (A) move RIM Next API behind api.rootedinmindfulness.org subdomain and set the NextAuth session cookie on .rootedinmindfulness.org so it is sent cross-subdomain; (B) token-based: member logs in via a Webflow-hosted form that calls /api/auth/signin-token, stores a short-lived JWT in localStorage, sends it as Authorization: Bearer on each member API call; (C) iframe + postMessage hand-shake. Option A is the cleanest production model and unblocks the broader member-area migration (dashboard, my-programs, registration, settings) — do this one right once and every future member feature on Webflow rides on it. Option B is a faster bootstrap if subdomain change is blocked. Include CORS + credentials:true configuration on all /api/member/* routes and an allowlist of Webflow origins. Test matrix: four guest states (current), four member states, logout transitions, deadline crossing (registrationClosed flipping mid-session).
notes: Builds on the single-placeholder CTA pattern established in session 92 (ctaHtml on /api/public/programs/[slug], one placeholder Block in Webflow). The auth-bridge decision is load-bearing for every Webflow member feature — draft and confirm with Jesse before implementing. Good candidate for a dedicated design session rather than ad-hoc work.

title: Dedup Aside blocks in migrated program descriptions
description: The session-91 fold_special_notes_into_description_as_aside migration prepended an Aside to each program's description, but at least one program (Awakening The Heart) already contained a manually-added Aside from session-90 testing — producing two identical Aside boxes on the public page. Need a one-time dedup migration that walks each program's description, detects consecutive or identical Aside blocks (by comparing normalized child content), and removes the duplicates. Low risk: only acts on programs with the duplication pattern. Also worth adding as a forward-guard in future field-sunset migrations: scan the destination field for an existing matching block before prepending, so this pattern can't recur for Announcement / EarlyArrival / DanaInvitation / etc.
notes: Interim fix available: authors can manually delete the duplicate Aside in the Program Editor's Content tab. Dedup migration only needed if the duplication turns out to affect several programs.

title: Member Program Detail Page
description: Create an authenticated /account/programs/[slug] page that serves as a member's personal view of a program they're registered for or have access to. Replaces the current pattern where the dashboard links to the public marketing page. Should include: registration status, Zoom/join link, calendar links (Google/Apple), pending actions (complete dana, update info), program logistics (next session date/time, location). Future: announcements, materials, form updates, host info.
notes: Dashboard currently links to public /programs/[slug] which is awkward for registered members. This page would be the inside-the-building view vs the storefront window.

title: Facilitator Profile Links
description: Link facilitators on program detail pages to User records with photos and short bios. Currently facilitators are stored as String[] (plain text names) with no avatar or profile link. Requires: connecting facilitator names to User records, displaying teacher profile photos (60px circular), linking to public teacher profile pages where they exist.
notes: Old Webflow site had circular photos next to facilitator names. Data model change needed — may link to existing teacherProfile records.

title: Redesign Remaining Legacy Pages
description: ~15 pages still reference Webflow class names via the legacy shim. Each needs an individual design pass to replace Webflow classes with prefixed design-system classes. Priority: Donate, Volunteer, Community Membership, Login. Lower priority: Diversity, Kalyana Mitta, Glossary, Magazine Articles.
notes: Legacy shim at bottom of custom.css can be deleted once all pages are migrated. Homepage and community programs page are done (session 84).

title: Admin File Manager — /admin/files
description: Build an admin page that shows every file uploaded via editors (Vercel Blob), grouped by where it lives in the app: hub documents, lessons, program descriptions, course descriptions, etc. Should display: total count and storage size, per-file location (which document / hub / program references it), size, upload date, and a clear 'orphans' section — blobs that exist in storage but are not referenced by any DB row. Each orphan gets a Delete button; bulk-delete-orphans for the common case. Also: wrap all content-bearing update/delete API routes in a shared `withContentCleanup()` helper so blob cleanup can't be forgotten when new editor surfaces are added.
notes: Currently cleanupRemovedBlobs/cleanupAllBlobs is wired only in hub/[slug]/documents and lessons routes. Program descriptions, manual sections, hub announcements, support replies do not clean up attachments on delete, so those can leak. The page would make leaks visible instantly and expose storage cost. Optional follow-up: a weekly cron that auto-sweeps orphans older than 24h.

title: Rich Callouts — container blocks with preset variants
description: Rebuild the callout as a container block (BlockNote spec with children) so the body supports lists, numbered steps, and nested paragraphs — not just inline marks. Keep variants as a curated preset list (no user-picked icons) so each variant carries a consistent meaning.
notes: Built in session 87 — but not as a single six-variant Callout. Split into five distinct editorial elements: Pull Quote, Verse Quote, Practice Suggestion (container), Reflection (container), and Note/Decision Callout (container). Rationale: each role deserves its own visual vocabulary, not a shared box with different accent colors. Container-body pattern (content: none + children) and defensive migration seeding are in place for all three container blocks.

title: Migrate Program specialNotes into SpecialNote block
description: Part of Stage 2d of the editor reorg (session 89). Program.specialNotes becomes a SpecialNote block inserted inline in Program.description. Field sunset, separate .pg-notes render slot removed. Data migration converts existing specialNotes JSON to a SpecialNote block appended to description.
notes: Superseded by the Stage 2d block-migration plan in UP_NEXT.md. SpecialNote is the first block we'll design together through the four-phase procedure in RIM_Editor_Types.md. Once that block exists, this migration becomes the template for Program.specialAnnouncement, Program.earlyArrivalMessage, Program.pullQuote pair, on-page Program.danaMessage, Lesson.headerQuote pair, and Lesson.reflectionPrompt.

title: <EditorField> terminal gate wrapper
description: After Stage 2d settles, build an <EditorField type='...' placement='...' /> wrapper that refuses to mount when placement is not in PLACEMENT_TYPE. Internally picks RimBlockEditor or RimProseEditor (with variant) based on type. All existing direct RimProseEditor / RimBlockEditor usages migrate to this wrapper. Makes the editor registry a compile-time + runtime gate rather than a polite request.
notes: Terminal piece of the editor reorg started in session 89. Referenced in RIM_Editor_Types.md and working-together-design-systems memory. Do this once placements stabilize through Stage 2d — not before, since a wrapper built on moving placements has to be rebuilt.

title: Migrate Sanity glossary to Postgres GlossaryTerm (Page Designer)
description: Part of Stage 2d. Glossary moves from Sanity to Postgres. Template data: name, slug, pali, sanskrit, synonyms. New body: Json? field as Page Designer — third Page Designer placement after program-description and lesson. Jesse noted the fields themselves may be modified during migration (etymology, relatedTerms, firstAppearance, etc.) — design that as part of the migration session.
notes: Output wrapper: rim-content rim-content--glossary gloss-body. Migration script follows the pattern used for programs (session 50/54) and lessons (session 72-78): Portable Text → BlockNote JSON with custom block conversions. Remove glossary* queries from lib/queries.ts after migration.

title: Migrate Sanity volunteerPositions to Postgres VolunteerPosition (Message)
description: Part of Stage 2d. volunteerPositions moves from Sanity to Postgres. Template data: name, slug, isOpen, currentVolunteers (FK to User). positionDescription: Json? as Message editor. Current Volunteers section returns on the page, linking to /teachers/[slug] for users with TeacherProfile.
notes: Output wrapper: rim-content vp-body. The 'Current Volunteers' section was removed from /volunteer-positions/[slug] in session 89 (it linked to the deleted Sanity teams pages); it returns post-migration with Postgres User relations. Remove volunteerPosition* queries from lib/queries.ts after migration.

title: SubClaim.message UI in host schedule claim flow
description: The SubClaim.message schema field exists but has no UI. Add an optional message textarea / RimProseEditor variant=compact to the 'I can cover this session' two-tap confirm in HubScheduleClient. Message POSTs through the existing claim API route, gets embedded in the sub-claimed notification email to the original host. Registered as sub-claim-message placement in session 89.
notes: Small feature — schema and email template are already wired. Only missing piece is the form field on the claim confirmation dialog. Registered placement sub-claim-message exists in lib/editorRegistry.ts with type=message.

title: Add shortName field to Program model
description: The Host Schedule calendar shows up to three program-name pills per day cell at ~12px font in ~110px-wide cells. Names longer than ~18 characters truncate with an ellipsis (e.g. 'Private Teacher Meetings' becomes 'Private Teach…'). Add an optional `shortName` field to the Program model so admins can set a readable abbreviation ('Private Teacher', 'Silent Meditation', 'Awakening'). The calendar pill display would use `shortName || name` with existing truncation as a fallback.
notes: Raised during session 88 Host Schedule redesign. Fields to update: Prisma Program model (new optional String), prisma/migrate.mjs (new idempotent migration), Program Editor Content tab (new input), `pillLabel()` function in `components/HubScheduleClient.tsx` (prefer shortName when present). No schema dependency since field is optional.

title: Architectural question: Step In gate vs. automatic host capability for all host-team members
description: Current model: host-team members who are not the assigned host must explicitly click 'Step in as Host' to gain host controls in the LiveKit session room. Simpler model: any active host-team HubMember automatically receives host token grants, removing the Step In gate entirely. The role design's two-host ideal — one host on the relational side, one on the technical — arguably fits the simpler model better: both should have controls from the moment they join. Tradeoffs: simpler model reduces friction and better matches a small trusted team; explicit Step In preserves responsibility clarity (one named host, others are guests who can upgrade). Decision should be made post-cutover unless training surfaces friction with the current model first.
notes: Surfaced during T2 (session room chapter, session 105). The Step In button is wired in app/session/[slug]/page.tsx — isHostTeam && !isHost conditional renders it. Token grant logic is in app/api/livekit/token/route.ts. If the simpler model is chosen, the Step In button and /api/livekit/step-in route can be removed.

title: Mobile audit for remaining hub tools and pages
description: Session 88 discovered that app/layout.tsx was missing a viewport meta tag — every route on the site had been rendering at ~980px desktop width on mobile and ignoring every @media (max-width: 768px) rule in custom.css. Viewport meta is now in place, which means existing mobile styles finally fire. Host Schedule got a focused mobile-friendliness pass (44px touch targets, iOS 16px input fix, chrome compression, two-tap confirm). Other hub tools and internal hub pages need the same treatment: /tools/programs, /tools/learning, /account/hub/[slug]/conversations, /account/hub/[slug]/documents, /account/hub/[slug]/members, /account/hub/[slug]/trash. Public pages (homepage, /community-programs, /this-week, /teachers, /courses, /programs/[slug], /lessons/[slug]) should also be re-tested — they weren't using their mobile styles either.
notes: Pattern to apply per tool: 44px touch targets on buttons/links, 16px font on text inputs (.fi/.ft/.fs already fixed globally at <768px), chrome compression for short viewports, defensive max-width on cards. Use the hub-schedule CSS block (~11915 in custom.css) as a reference pattern.
